q: Under the pre-merger financial convention, a railway paid a dividend of Rs 600 crore to General Finances at the rate of 5 per cent per annum. The capital-at-charge of the railway (excluding the capital invested in strategic lines) was:

options.A: Rs 10,000 crore
options.B: Rs 15,000 crore
options.D: Rs 12,000 crore

e: Capital-at-charge = dividend / rate = 600 / 5 per cent = Rs 12,000 crore, since dividend was charged only on the capital excluding strategic lines.

q: The total expenditure of the Government of India for a year is Rs 60,00,000 crore, its revenue receipts are Rs 42,00,000 crore and its non-debt capital receipts (recoveries of loans and disinvestment proceeds) are Rs 2,50,000 crore. The fiscal deficit of the Government for the year is:

options.A: Rs 18,00,000 crore
options.B: Rs 15,50,000 crore
options.D: Rs 15,00,000 crore

e: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure - revenue receipts - non-debt capital receipts = 60,00,000 - 42,00,000 - 2,50,000 = Rs 15,50,000 crore.

q: The fiscal deficit of the Government of India for a year is Rs 16,80,000 crore and the interest payments during the year are Rs 9,40,000 crore. The primary deficit of the Government for the year is:

options.A: Rs 7,40,000 crore
options.B: Rs 7,20,000 crore
options.D: Rs 8,40,000 crore

e: Primary deficit = fiscal deficit - interest payments = 16,80,000 - 9,40,000 = Rs 7,40,000 crore.

q: The revenue receipts of the Government of India for a year are Rs 28,00,000 crore and its revenue expenditure is Rs 36,40,000 crore. The revenue deficit of the Government for the year is:

options.A: Rs 7,40,000 crore
options.B: Rs 8,00,000 crore
options.D: Rs 8,40,000 crore

e: Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure - revenue receipts = 36,40,000 - 28,00,000 = Rs 8,40,000 crore.

q: The total debt of the Central Government is Rs 1,05,00,000 crore and the Gross Domestic Product of the country is Rs 3,00,00,000 crore. The debt-to-GDP ratio of the Central Government is:

options.A: 30 per cent
options.B: 33.5 per cent
options.D: 37.5 per cent

e: Debt-to-GDP ratio = total debt / GDP x 100 = 1,05,00,000 / 3,00,00,000 x 100 = 35 per cent.

q: Under Article 288 of the Constitution, a law of a State imposing a tax in respect of water or electricity stored, generated, consumed, distributed or sold by an authority established for regulating or developing an inter-State river or river-valley can have effect only if it has:

options.A: Been approved by the Finance Commission
options.B: Been reserved for the consideration of the President and has received his assent
options.C: Been approved by the Rajya Sabha by a special majority
options.D: Been concurred in by all the States through whose territory the river flows

e: Under Article 288, such a State law imposing a tax on water or electricity of an inter-State river authority can have effect only if it has been reserved for the consideration of the President and has received his assent.

q: Under Article 290 of the Constitution, where a court, commission or tribunal serves the needs of both the Union and a State, the expenses thereof are to be shared between the Union and the State as may be agreed between them, and failing agreement, as determined by:

options.A: The Finance Commission
options.B: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: An arbitrator appointed by the Chief Justice of India

e: Under Article 290, failing agreement between the Union and the State, the sharing of such expenses is determined by an arbitrator appointed by the Chief Justice of India.

q: The administrative expenses of a High Court, including all salaries, allowances and pensions payable to or in respect of the officers and servants of the Court, are charged on:

options.A: The Consolidated Fund of the State
options.B: The Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: The Contingency Fund of the State
options.D: The Public Account of the State

e: The administrative expenses of a High Court, including salaries, allowances and pensions of its officers and servants, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.

q: In the Legislature of a State, no demand for a grant shall be made except on the recommendation of:

options.A: The Finance Minister of the State
options.B: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
options.D: The Finance Commission

e: In the Legislature of a State, no demand for a grant can be made except on the recommendation of the Governor of the State.

q: Taxes on railway fares and freights, along with terminal taxes on goods or passengers carried by railway, sea or air, are enumerated in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution under:

options.A: Entry 22
options.B: Entry 89
options.D: Entry 97

e: Taxes on railway fares and freights, along with terminal taxes on goods or passengers carried by railway, sea or air, are enumerated in the Union List under Entry 89.

q: Which of the following pairs of Parliamentary Committees are popularly described as 'twin sisters'?

options.A: The Public Accounts Committee and the Estimates Committee
options.B: The Estimates Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings
options.C: The Public Accounts Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings
options.D: The Railway Convention Committee and the Public Accounts Committee

e: The Public Accounts Committee and the Estimates Committee are popularly called twin sisters, as both are financial committees of Parliament exercising continuing scrutiny over public expenditure and economy.

q: The Finance Commission of India is often described as:

options.A: An executive agency of the Ministry of Finance
options.B: A permanent body of Parliament
options.C: A tribunal whose recommendations are binding on the Government
options.D: A quasi-judicial body

e: The Finance Commission is often described as a quasi-judicial body because it functions impartially, in the manner of a tribunal, while deciding on the distribution of revenues between the Union and the States.

q: The 'total liabilities' of the Central Government, as presented in the Budget documents, comprise:

options.A: Only the internal debt of the Government
options.B: Only the internal and external debt of the Government
options.C: Internal debt, external debt and other liabilities, including the liabilities under the Public Account
options.D: Internal debt and the balances of the reserve funds of the Railways

e: The total liabilities of the Central Government comprise internal debt, external debt and other liabilities, including the liabilities under the Public Account such as small savings and provident funds.

q: Capital receipts of the Government of India are those receipts which:

options.A: Are received regularly every year in the course of its operations
options.B: Either create a liability for the Government or result in a reduction of its financial assets
options.C: Do not form part of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: Are required to be voted by Parliament

e: Capital receipts are those receipts which either create a liability for the Government, such as borrowings, or result in a reduction of its financial assets, such as disinvestment proceeds and recoveries of loans.

q: If the primary deficit of the Government of India for a year is zero, it implies that:

options.A: The borrowings of the Government during the year are being used only to meet its interest payments
options.B: The Government has not resorted to any borrowing during the year
options.C: The revenue receipts of the Government are equal to its revenue expenditure
options.D: The fiscal deficit of the Government for the year is also zero

e: Primary deficit is the fiscal deficit minus interest payments; a zero primary deficit means the fiscal deficit equals interest payments, so the year's borrowings are used only to meet interest payments.

q: The accounts of external assistance, that is, grants and loans received from foreign governments and multilateral agencies, are maintained, and disbursements against them authorised, by:

options.A: The Reserve Bank of India
options.B: The Controller General of Accounts
options.C: The Controller of Aid, Accounts and Audit in the Department of Economic Affairs
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: The accounts of external assistance, grants and loans from foreign governments and multilateral agencies, are maintained, and disbursements against them authorised, by the Controller of Aid, Accounts and Audit in the Department of Economic Affairs.

q: The first Budget in India was presented in the year 1860 by:

options.A: R. K. Shanmukham Chetty
options.B: John Mathai
options.D: James Wilson

e: The first Budget in India was presented in the year 1860 by James Wilson, the first Finance Member of the Government of India.

q: The practice of presenting the Union Budget at 5 p.m. was given up, and the Budget began to be presented at 11 a.m., with effect from the Budget for:
e: The practice of presenting the Union Budget at 5 p.m. was given up and presentation at 11 a.m. began with the Budget for 2001-02.

q: Part B of the Budget Speech of the Finance Minister deals with:

options.A: The state of the economy and the policy initiatives of the Government
options.B: The review of the working of the public sector undertakings
options.C: The taxation proposals of the Government for the ensuing year
options.D: The demands for grants of the various Ministries

e: Part B of the Budget Speech of the Finance Minister deals with the taxation proposals of the Government for the ensuing year, while Part A covers the state of the economy and policy initiatives.

q: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation, the market-borrowing arm of the Ministry of Railways, was incorporated in the year:
e: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation, the market-borrowing arm of the Ministry of Railways, was incorporated in the year 1986.

q: The obligation of the Reserve Bank of India to transact the general banking business of the Government of India flows from:

options.A: Section 21A of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
options.B: Section 45 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
options.D: Section 21 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934

e: The obligation of the Reserve Bank of India to transact the general banking business of the Government of India flows from Section 21 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

q: Advances made by the Reserve Bank of India to the Central and State Governments by way of Ways and Means Advances are, in each case, repayable not later than:

options.A: Six months from the date of the advance
options.B: Three months from the date of the advance
options.C: The close of the financial year in which the advance is made
options.D: Twelve months from the date of the advance

e: Ways and Means Advances made by the Reserve Bank of India to the Central and State Governments are repayable not later than three months from the date of the advance.

q: In the case of a Government company, the statutory auditor is appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India within a period of:

options.A: 60 days from the commencement of the financial year
options.B: 30 days from the commencement of the financial year
options.C: 180 days from the commencement of the financial year
options.D: 90 days from the commencement of the financial year

e: In the case of a Government company, the statutory auditor is appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India within 180 days from the commencement of the financial year.

q: Under the Companies Act, 2013, where a company is a subsidiary of a Government company, such subsidiary company is:

options.A: Also treated as a Government company
options.B: Treated as a Government company only if the Government holds shares in it directly
options.C: Not treated as a Government company
options.D: Treated as a Government company only with the approval of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Under the Companies Act, 2013, a subsidiary of a Government company is itself treated as a Government company, whether or not the Government holds shares in it directly.

q: Under the ISSAI framework of INTOSAI, ISSAI 130 sets out:

options.A: The fundamental principles of financial audit
options.B: The principles of transparency and accountability of Supreme Audit Institutions
options.C: The fundamental principles of performance audit
options.D: The Code of Ethics for public-sector auditing

e: Under the ISSAI framework, ISSAI 130 sets out the Code of Ethics for public-sector auditing.

q: Under the ISSAI framework of INTOSAI, ISSAI 140 deals with:

options.A: The audit of public debt
options.B: Quality control for Supreme Audit Institutions
options.D: Environmental auditing

e: Under the ISSAI framework, ISSAI 140 deals with quality control for Supreme Audit Institutions.

q: Under the framework originally laid down for the National Investment Fund, the income of the Fund was required to be utilised in the following manner:

options.A: The whole of it for capital investment in public sector undertakings
options.B: One-half for social sector schemes and one-half for capital investment in public sector undertakings
options.C: 75 per cent for financing social sector schemes and 25 per cent for capital investment in public sector undertakings
options.D: The whole of it for financing social sector schemes

e: Under the original National Investment Fund framework, 75 per cent of the income of the Fund was to finance social sector schemes and 25 per cent was for capital investment in public sector undertakings.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended that the share of the States in the net proceeds of the divisible pool of central taxes should be 41 per cent, as against the 42 per cent recommended by the Fourteenth Finance Commission.
2. The reduction of one percentage point was made to provide for the resources of the newly created Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, which are met by the Centre.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. The Fifteenth Finance Commission reduced the States' share from 42 to 41 per cent, retaining one percentage point for the resources of the new Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, which are met by the Centre.

q: In the accounts of the Government of India, the dividends and profits received from public sector undertakings and other investments are classified under Major Head:
e: In the accounts of the Government of India, dividends and profits received from public sector undertakings and other investments are classified under Major Head 0050.

q: The Outcome Budget, presenting the financial outlays of the Ministries along with the physical outcomes expected from them, was first presented to Parliament with the Union Budget for:
e: The Outcome Budget, presenting the financial outlays of the Ministries along with the physical outcomes expected from them, was first presented to Parliament with the Union Budget for 2005-06.

q: The Acworth Committee, whose recommendations led to the separation of Railway finances from the general finances of the Government of India, was appointed in the year:
e: The Acworth Committee, whose recommendations led to the separation of Railway finances from the general finances of the Government of India, was appointed in the year 1920.

q: The creation of the Railway Board was recommended by:

options.A: The Acworth Committee
options.B: The Kunzru Committee
options.D: The Wedgwood Committee

e: The creation of the Railway Board was recommended by the Robertson Committee.

q: Under Article 279A(4) of the Constitution, the Goods and Services Tax Council may make recommendations to the Union and the States on, among other things:

options.A: A special rate or rates, for a specified period, to raise additional resources during any natural calamity or disaster
options.B: The exemption of specified goods from the purview of the Goods and Services Tax for an indefinite period
options.C: The sharing of the proceeds of the Goods and Services Tax between the Union and the States
options.D: The compensation payable to the States for loss of revenue on account of the introduction of the Goods and Services Tax

e: Under Article 279A(4), the Goods and Services Tax Council may recommend a special rate or rates, for a specified period, to raise additional resources during any natural calamity or disaster.

q: Under the 'escape clause' of the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management framework, a deviation from the fiscal deficit target may be sought, among others, on the ground of:

options.A: A shortfall in the disinvestment receipts of the Government
options.B: A collapse of agriculture severely impacting farm output and incomes
options.C: An increase in the subsidy bill of the Government
options.D: A decline in the collections of the Goods and Services Tax

e: Under the escape clause of the FRBM framework, deviation from the fiscal deficit target may be sought, among other grounds, on a collapse of agriculture severely impacting farm output and incomes.

q: In a financial (attest) audit, a 'qualified opinion' is expressed by the auditor when:

options.A: The financial statements are free from any misstatement whatsoever
options.B: The auditor is unable to obtain any evidence whatsoever for the audit
options.C: The misstatements in the financial statements are both material and pervasive
options.D: The misstatements in the financial statements are material, but not pervasive

e: A qualified opinion is expressed when the misstatements in the financial statements are material but not pervasive, so the opinion is modified only to that extent.

q: A zonal railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 8,800 crore, ordinary working expenses of Rs 5,720 crore, appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund of Rs 440 crore and appropriation to the Pension Fund of Rs 440 crore. Its Operating Ratio is:

options.A: 65 per cent
options.B: 70 per cent
options.D: 80 per cent

e: Working expenses = 5,720 + 440 + 440 = Rs 6,600 crore. Operating Ratio = 6,600 / 8,800 x 100 = 75 per cent.

q: A zonal railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 5,200 crore, ordinary working expenses of Rs 4,940 crore, appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund of Rs 260 crore and appropriation to the Pension Fund of Rs 260 crore. Its Operating Ratio is:

options.A: 95 per cent
options.B: 105 per cent
options.D: 110 per cent

e: Working expenses = 4,940 + 260 + 260 = Rs 5,460 crore. Operating Ratio = 5,460 / 5,200 x 100 = 105 per cent, expenses exceeding earnings.

q: A railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 5,600 crore and working expenses, including appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, of Rs 4,480 crore. Its net revenue is:

options.A: Rs 1,120 crore
options.B: Rs 1,020 crore
options.D: Rs 980 crore

e: Net revenue = gross traffic earnings - working expenses = 5,600 - 4,480 = Rs 1,120 crore.

q: A railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 6,800 crore, working expenses, including appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, of Rs 5,780 crore and dividend payable to General Finances of Rs 420 crore. Its surplus is:

options.A: Rs 1,020 crore
options.B: Rs 720 crore
options.D: Rs 600 crore

e: Net revenue = 6,800 - 5,780 = Rs 1,020 crore. Surplus = net revenue - dividend = 1,020 - 420 = Rs 600 crore.

q: The net revenue of a railway is Rs 1,870 crore and its capital-at-charge is Rs 34,000 crore. The return on capital-at-charge of the railway is:

options.A: 5.0 per cent
options.B: 5.5 per cent
options.D: 6.5 per cent

e: Return on capital-at-charge = 1,870 / 34,000 x 100 = 5.5 per cent.

q: Under the pre-merger financial convention, the capital-at-charge of a railway is Rs 30,000 crore, which includes Rs 2,000 crore invested in strategic lines. Dividend is payable to General Finances at the rate of 5 per cent per annum only on the capital-at-charge excluding the capital invested in strategic lines. The dividend payable by the railway is:

options.A: Rs 1,500 crore
options.B: Rs 1,300 crore
options.D: Rs 1,600 crore

e: Dividend is charged only on capital excluding strategic lines: 5 per cent of (30,000 - 2,000) = 5 per cent of Rs 28,000 crore = Rs 1,400 crore.

q: Under the pre-merger financial convention, a railway earned a net revenue of Rs 1,950 crore, which represented a return of 7.5 per cent on its capital-at-charge. The capital-at-charge of the railway was:

options.A: Rs 26,000 crore
options.B: Rs 24,000 crore
options.D: Rs 30,000 crore

e: Capital-at-charge = net revenue / return rate = 1,950 / 7.5 per cent = Rs 26,000 crore.

q: The total expenditure of the Government of India for a year is Rs 55,00,000 crore, its revenue receipts are Rs 40,00,000 crore and its non-debt capital receipts (recoveries of loans and disinvestment proceeds) are Rs 1,20,000 crore. The fiscal deficit of the Government for the year is:

options.A: Rs 15,00,000 crore
options.B: Rs 13,60,000 crore
options.D: Rs 13,80,000 crore

e: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure - revenue receipts - non-debt capital receipts = 55,00,000 - 40,00,000 - 1,20,000 = Rs 13,80,000 crore.

q: The fiscal deficit of the Government of India for a year is Rs 12,40,000 crore and the interest payments during the year are Rs 7,10,000 crore. The primary deficit of the Government for the year is:

options.A: Rs 5,10,000 crore
options.B: Rs 5,30,000 crore
options.D: Rs 4,90,000 crore

e: Primary deficit = fiscal deficit - interest payments = 12,40,000 - 7,10,000 = Rs 5,30,000 crore.

q: The revenue receipts of the Government of India for a year are Rs 30,50,000 crore and its revenue expenditure is Rs 39,25,000 crore. The revenue deficit of the Government for the year is:

options.A: Rs 8,25,000 crore
options.B: Rs 9,25,000 crore
options.D: Rs 8,50,000 crore

e: Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure - revenue receipts = 39,25,000 - 30,50,000 = Rs 8,75,000 crore.

q: The revenue deficit of the Government of India for a year is Rs 5,40,000 crore and the grants given to the States and others for the creation of capital assets during the year are Rs 1,60,000 crore. The effective revenue deficit of the Government for the year is:

options.A: Rs 3,80,000 crore
options.B: Rs 4,20,000 crore
options.D: Rs 4,00,000 crore

e: Effective revenue deficit = revenue deficit - grants for creation of capital assets = 5,40,000 - 1,60,000 = Rs 3,80,000 crore.

q: The fiscal deficit of the Government of India for a year is Rs 19,80,000 crore and the Gross Domestic Product of the country for the year is Rs 3,30,00,000 crore. The fiscal deficit as a percentage of the Gross Domestic Product is:

options.A: 5.0 per cent
options.B: 5.5 per cent
options.D: 6.0 per cent

e: Fiscal deficit as a percentage of GDP = 19,80,000 / 3,30,00,000 x 100 = 6.0 per cent.

q: The divisible pool of central taxes for a year is Rs 10,00,000 crore. Applying the share of 41 per cent recommended by the Fifteenth Finance Commission, the aggregate amount devolving to the States out of the divisible pool is:

options.A: Rs 4,20,000 crore
options.B: Rs 4,00,000 crore
options.D: Rs 4,10,000 crore

e: Aggregate devolution to the States = 41 per cent of the divisible pool of Rs 10,00,000 crore = Rs 4,10,000 crore.

q: The revenue of a State from the taxes subsumed in the Goods and Services Tax in the base year 2015-16 was Rs 40,000 crore. Projecting this revenue at the assured growth rate of 14 per cent, the protected revenue of the State for the year 2016-17 works out as per the Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act, 2017. If the actual revenue of the State for 2016-17 was Rs 43,600 crore, the compensation payable to the State is:

options.A: Rs 1,600 crore
options.B: Rs 2,400 crore
options.D: Rs 3,600 crore

e: Protected revenue = 40,000 x 1.14 = Rs 45,600 crore. Compensation = protected revenue - actual revenue = 45,600 - 43,600 = Rs 2,000 crore.

q: The capital expenditure of the Government of India for a year is Rs 8,50,000 crore and the grants-in-aid given by it during the year for the creation of capital assets are Rs 2,30,000 crore. The Effective Capital Expenditure of the Government for the year is:

options.A: Rs 10,80,000 crore
options.B: Rs 6,20,000 crore
options.D: Rs 11,10,000 crore

e: Effective Capital Expenditure = capital expenditure + grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets = 8,50,000 + 2,30,000 = Rs 10,80,000 crore.

q: Lines which are constructed and worked on commercial considerations, that is, in the expectation of earning an adequate return on the capital invested in them, are known as:

options.A: Strategic lines
options.B: Subsidised lines
options.D: Departmental lines

e: Lines built and worked on commercial considerations, in the expectation of earning an adequate return on the capital invested, are classified as commercial lines, as distinct from strategic lines built for defence and subsidised lines.

q: Government accounts, kept on the classification and cash basis, do not by themselves reveal the profit or loss of a commercial undertaking. Commercial accounts are additionally maintained for Indian Railways mainly to:

options.A: Replace the Government accounts altogether
options.B: Ascertain the commercial results and the financial position of the undertaking
options.C: Avoid audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Satisfy the requirements of the Reserve Bank of India

e: Government accounts on the cash and classification basis show only receipts and payments, not profit or loss, so Railways additionally maintain commercial accounts to ascertain the commercial results and the financial position of the undertaking.

q: Which of the following is a recognised canon of financial propriety?

options.A: No authority should exercise its powers of sanctioning expenditure to pass an order which will be directly or indirectly to its own advantage
options.B: An authority may sanction expenditure which benefits itself, provided the amount is small
options.C: Allowances granted to meet expenditure of a particular type may be a source of profit to the recipients
options.D: Savings under a grant may be retained by the sanctioning authority for use in the following year

e: A canon of financial propriety in the General Financial Rules is that no authority should sanction expenditure by an order which will be directly or indirectly to its own advantage; self-benefiting sanctions are prohibited.

q: Under the canons of financial propriety, public moneys should not ordinarily be utilised for the benefit of a particular person or a section of the people unless:

options.A: The amount involved is large
options.B: The sanctioning officer considers it desirable
options.C: The contractor or beneficiary concerned so requests
options.D: The claim could be enforced in a court of law, or the expenditure is in pursuance of a recognised policy or custom

e: Under the canons of financial propriety, public moneys should not ordinarily be used for a particular person or section unless the claim could be enforced in a court of law or the expenditure follows a recognised policy or custom.

q: A 'token cut' motion in the Lok Sabha is moved primarily to:

options.A: Ventilate a specific grievance which is within the scope of the demand
options.B: Disapprove the policy underlying the demand
options.C: Effect a specified economy in the expenditure
options.D: Reduce the demand to one-half of the amount proposed

e: A token cut motion seeks a nominal reduction of Rs 100 in a demand and is moved primarily to ventilate a specific grievance within the scope of the demand, unlike a policy cut or an economy cut.

q: In terms of membership, the largest committee of Parliament among the following is the:

options.A: Public Accounts Committee
options.B: Committee on Public Undertakings
options.D: Estimates Committee

e: The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha, making it the largest parliamentary committee among those listed; the Public Accounts Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings have 22 each.

q: The members of the Railway Convention Committee are drawn from:

options.A: The Lok Sabha only
options.B: The Rajya Sabha only
options.D: The State Legislatures

e: The Railway Convention Committee is a joint committee of Parliament, so its members are drawn from both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Appropriation Act from the Appropriation Accounts?

options.A: The Appropriation Act authorises withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of India for a year, while the Appropriation Accounts compare the actual expenditure of the year with the final grants and appropriations after the close of the year
options.B: The Appropriation Act compares actual expenditure with the grants, while the Appropriation Accounts authorise withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Both the Appropriation Act and the Appropriation Accounts are prepared after the close of the financial year
options.D: The Appropriation Accounts are passed by Parliament before the Demands for Grants are voted

e: The Appropriation Act is the law passed by Parliament authorising withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund up to the amounts granted. The Appropriation Accounts are prepared after the year comparing actual expenditure with the final grant, so option D is correct.

q: Parliamentary control over public expenditure at the stage before the expenditure is incurred is exercised mainly through:

options.A: Examination of the accounts by the Public Accounts Committee
options.B: The Action Taken Notes furnished by the Government
options.C: The Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Discussion and voting of the Demands for Grants and the passing of the Appropriation Act

e: Parliamentary control before expenditure is incurred is exercised ex ante through discussion and voting of the Demands for Grants and passing of the Appropriation Act; committee examination of accounts and CAG reports operates after the expenditure.

q: Which of the following correctly brings out the distinction between the Public Accounts Committee and the Estimates Committee in relation to policy?

options.A: The Public Accounts Committee suggests alternative policies, while the Estimates Committee does not go into questions of policy
options.B: The Public Accounts Committee frames the policy underlying each demand, while the Estimates Committee only checks the accounts
options.C: The Public Accounts Committee does not go into questions of policy, while the Estimates Committee may suggest alternative policies in order to bring about efficiency and economy in administration
options.D: Neither Committee can make any suggestion touching policy or economy

e: The Public Accounts Committee examines accounts after expenditure and does not go into questions of policy, while the Estimates Committee may suggest alternative policies to bring about efficiency and economy in administration.

q: Prompt clearance of suspense balances is insisted upon because, so long as transactions remain under suspense heads:

options.A: The accounts do not reflect the true and final position of the receipts and expenditure concerned
options.B: Interest becomes payable on the balances
options.C: The balances lapse at the close of the year
options.D: Audit of the accounts is dispensed with

e: Suspense heads are only temporary, intermediate heads, so until they are cleared the transactions are not booked to their final heads and the accounts do not reflect the true and final position of the receipts and expenditure concerned.

q:
Consider the following statements about the review of suspense balances:
1. The review verifies that the balances are composed of genuine items awaiting final adjustment for valid reasons.
2. The review pursues the clearance of old outstanding items and fixes responsibility for their clearance.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Review of suspense balances serves both purposes: it verifies that balances consist of genuine items awaiting final adjustment for valid reasons, and it pursues clearance of old outstandings and fixes responsibility for clearance, so both statements are correct.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a suspense head from a remittance head?

options.A: A suspense head accounts for transactions in transit between two accounting circles, while a remittance head is operated when the final head is not known
options.B: There is no difference between a suspense head and a remittance head
options.C: A remittance head is operated only for transactions with foreign Governments, while a suspense head is operated for all other transactions
options.D: A suspense head is operated when a transaction cannot for the time being be booked to its final head, while a remittance head accounts for transactions in transit between accounting circles or offices

e: A suspense head is operated when a transaction cannot for the time being be booked to its final head for want of particulars, while a remittance head accounts for transactions in transit between accounting circles or offices, so statement D states the distinction correctly.

q: In the Government system of accounts, Suspense Accounts (Major Head 8658) form part of:

options.A: The Consolidated Fund of India — Revenue section
options.B: The Consolidated Fund of India — Capital section
options.D: The Contingency Fund of India

e: In the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, Major Head 8658 Suspense Accounts falls in the Public Account of India under the sector for Suspense and Miscellaneous, not in the Consolidated Fund or the Contingency Fund.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The resident audit organisation on a zonal Railway functions under the Comptroller and Auditor General of India and is independent of the Railway administration.
2. The audit programme of the Principal Director of Audit requires the approval of the FA&CAO of the Railway.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The resident audit organisation on a zonal Railway works under the CAG and is independent of the Railway administration, so statement 1 is correct; its audit programme does not require FA and CAO approval, so statement 2 is wrong.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes regulatory (compliance) audit from performance audit?

options.A: Regulatory audit examines the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of operations, while performance audit verifies conformity with rules
options.B: Regulatory audit verifies that transactions conform to the applicable rules, regulations and sanctions, while performance audit examines the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of operations
options.C: Regulatory audit is conducted by the internal audit organisation, while performance audit is conducted by the Accounts Department
options.D: There is no difference between the two

e: Regulatory or compliance audit verifies that transactions conform to the applicable rules, regulations and sanctions, while performance audit examines the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of operations, so option B states the distinction correctly.

q: A theme-based audit of a subject such as passenger amenities, taken up simultaneously on several zonal Railways, primarily enables Audit to:

options.A: Pass the bills of the units audited
options.B: Fix the fares and freight rates for the services concerned
options.C: Compile the accounts of the zonal Railways
options.D: Identify systemic and common weaknesses and make recommendations at the all-India level

e: A theme-based audit taken up simultaneously on several zonal Railways lets Audit compare results across Railways, identify systemic and common weaknesses and make recommendations at the all-India level.

q: The Manual of Standing Orders (Audit), which contains the standing instructions and principles governing the conduct of audit, is issued by:

options.A: The Railway Board
options.B: The office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Controller General of Accounts

e: The Manual of Standing Orders (Audit), containing the standing instructions and principles governing the conduct of audit, is issued by the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

q: Preliminary queries seeking information or clarification, raised by an audit party during the course of audit before objections are formalised, are issued in the form of:

options.A: Audit Memos
options.B: Draft Paras
options.D: Audit Paras

e: Audit Memos are the preliminary queries issued by an audit party during audit to seek information or clarification before objections are formalised as Inspection Reports, Draft Paras or Audit Paras.

q: In a financial (attest) audit, a disclaimer of opinion is expressed when:

options.A: The financial statements present a true and fair view
options.B: The misstatements are material but not pervasive
options.C: Only minor arithmetical errors are noticed in the accounts
options.D: The auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence and the possible effects of undetected misstatements could be both material and pervasive

e: In financial attest audit, a disclaimer of opinion is given when the auditor cannot obtain sufficient appropriate evidence and the possible effects of undetected misstatements could be both material and pervasive, so no opinion is expressed.

q: The statutory audit conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is in the nature of external audit essentially because:

options.A: It is conducted outside the premises of the audited office
options.B: The auditor is independent of, and not subordinate to, the organisation whose accounts are audited
options.C: It is conducted only after the close of the financial year
options.D: It is conducted by a private agency engaged on contract

e: CAG audit is external audit essentially because the CAG is constitutionally independent of, and not subordinate to, the organisation audited, not merely because of where or when the audit is conducted.

q:
Consider the following statements about the causes of unsanctioned expenditure:
1. It arises where expenditure is incurred in anticipation of sanction in urgent cases and the sanction is not received.
2. It arises where there is delay in according sanction, or revised sanction, by the competent authority.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Unsanctioned expenditure arises both where expenditure is incurred in anticipation of sanction in urgent cases and the sanction is not received, and where sanction or revised sanction is delayed by the competent authority, so both statements are correct.

q: Unsanctioned expenditure on Railways can be minimised mainly by:

options.A: Obtaining the sanction of the competent authority before incurring the expenditure, as a rule
options.B: Booking the expenditure under a suspense head
options.C: Presenting a token demand in the following year's Budget
options.D: Writing off the expenditure at the close of the year

e: Unsanctioned expenditure is minimised mainly by following the basic rule that the sanction of the competent authority is obtained before the expenditure is incurred.

q: The salaries of railway staff for March 2027 are paid in April 2027. Under the accrual system of accounting, this expenditure is recognised in the accounts of:

options.A: 2027-28, the year in which the payment is made
options.B: The year in which the bill is received from the staff
options.C: 2026-27, the year in which the salaries were earned and the liability was incurred
options.D: It is not recognised as expenditure at all

e: Under accrual accounting, expenditure is recognised in the period in which the liability is incurred, not when paid, so March 2027 salaries paid in April 2027 belong to 2026-27, the year in which they were earned.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the accrual system of accounting, depreciation on assets is charged in the accounts of the period.
2. Under the accrual system of accounting, provision is made for expenses incurred but not yet paid, that is, for outstanding liabilities.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Accrual accounting charges depreciation on assets in the period and also makes provision for expenses incurred but not yet paid, that is outstanding liabilities, so both statements are correct.

q: A principal objective of merging the Railway Budget with the General Budget was to:

options.A: Remove railway accounts from audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: Present a holistic and comprehensive picture of the finances of the Government of India
options.C: Dispense with the voting of the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways
options.D: Stop Gross Budgetary Support to Railways

e: A principal objective of merging the Railway Budget with the General Budget from 2017-18 was to present a holistic and comprehensive picture of the finances of the Government of India in one Budget.

q: Which of the following does NOT form part of the Extra Budgetary Resources (EBR) of Indian Railways?

options.A: Market borrowings raised through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation
options.B: Institutional finance raised for railway projects
options.C: Investment through public-private partnership for railway projects
options.D: Gross Budgetary Support provided through the Union Budget

e: Extra Budgetary Resources consist of market borrowings, institutional finance and PPP investment raised outside the Budget; Gross Budgetary Support is provided through the Union Budget itself, so it is not part of EBR.

q: A persistently rising Operating Ratio of a railway indicates that:

options.A: Working expenses are claiming a rising share of the gross traffic earnings, leaving a shrinking margin
options.B: The financial health of the railway is improving
options.C: The capital-at-charge of the railway is falling
options.D: The composition of traffic of the railway is improving

e: Operating Ratio is working expenses as a percentage of gross traffic earnings, so a persistently rising ratio means working expenses claim a rising share of earnings and leave a shrinking margin, indicating worsening financial health.

q: The separation of Railway finances from the general finances in 1924-25 was intended mainly to:

options.A: Merge the railway accounts with the accounts of the States
options.B: Secure stability and freedom for Railway finances, so that Railways could be managed on commercial lines
options.C: Abolish the dividend payable to General Finances
options.D: Dispense with the commercial accounts of Railways

e: The Separation Convention of 1924 separated Railway finances from general finances from 1924-25 mainly to secure stability and freedom for Railway finances so that Railways could be managed on commercial lines.

q: The financial relations between Indian Railways and the General Finances were governed by:

options.A: A statute enacted by Parliament for the purpose
options.B: A convention adopted through resolutions passed by Parliament from time to time
options.C: Orders issued by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The award of the Finance Commission

e: The financial relations between Railways and General Finances, including the dividend payable, were governed not by statute but by a convention adopted through resolutions passed by Parliament from time to time, on Railway Convention Committee recommendations.

q: A balance outstanding under a suspense head of account does NOT represent:

options.A: An amount awaiting final adjustment
options.B: An amount recoverable by, or adjustable in favour of, the Railway
options.C: A transaction which has not yet been booked to its final head
options.D: Final expenditure booked to a service or detailed head of account

e: A suspense balance is by definition an amount awaiting final adjustment, recoverable or adjustable, and not yet booked to its final head; it therefore does not represent final expenditure booked to a service or detailed head.

q: The ordinary working expenses of Indian Railways, accounted for under Major Head 3002, are charged to which section of the Consolidated Fund of India?

options.A: Revenue section
options.B: Capital section
options.D: Contingency Fund

e: Ordinary working expenses of Railways under Major Head 3002 are revenue expenditure and are charged to the Revenue section of the Consolidated Fund of India.

q: The topics taken up for performance audit are selected by:

options.A: The Ministry whose programmes are to be audited
options.B: The office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, on considerations of significance, risk and materiality
options.D: The Finance Commission

e: Topics for performance audit are selected by the office of the CAG itself, on considerations of significance, risk and materiality, and not by the Ministry audited, the Public Accounts Committee or the Finance Commission.

q: In the classification of Government accounts, transactions are classified primarily according to:

options.A: The department which incurs the expenditure
options.B: The officer who sanctions the expenditure
options.C: The source from which the funds are drawn
options.D: The function or programme of the Government to which the transactions relate

e: In the Government system of accounts, classification is primarily functional: transactions are classified according to the function or programme of Government to which they relate, reflected in the Major Head structure.

q: 'Deposits with Reserve Bank', a link head in the railway system of accounts, represents:

options.A: The cash balance of the Railways held with the Reserve Bank of India as part of the Government account
options.B: Deposits made by the public with the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: Loans advanced by the Reserve Bank of India to Railways
options.D: The Provident Fund deposits of railway employees

e: Deposits with Reserve Bank is the link head representing the cash balance of Railways held with the Reserve Bank of India as part of the Government account, through which railway cash transactions are adjusted.

q: In the Balance Sheet of Indian Railways, stores and materials held in stock are shown:

options.A: On the liabilities side
options.B: Only in the Public Account of India
options.D: Only in the Finance Accounts of the Union

e: In the Balance Sheet of Indian Railways, stores and materials held in stock are an asset of the undertaking and are therefore shown on the assets side.

q: The reports of the Public Accounts Committee are presented to:

options.A: Both Houses of Parliament
options.B: The President of India
options.D: The Lok Sabha

e: The Public Accounts Committee is a committee of the Lok Sabha (with Rajya Sabha members associated), and its reports are presented to the Lok Sabha.

q: A heavy rush of expenditure in the month of March is viewed in audit as indicating:

options.A: Defective budgetary control and poor planning of the flow of expenditure during the year
options.B: Sound and economical financial management
options.C: That an Excess Grant will invariably be required
options.D: That the grant for the year was inadequate

e: A heavy rush of expenditure in March is an audit objection because it indicates defective budgetary control and poor planning of the flow of expenditure evenly through the year, often to avoid lapse of grant.

q: Expenditure incurred in excess of a charged appropriation on the Consolidated Fund of India:

options.A: Requires no regularisation, as charged expenditure is not voted by Parliament
options.B: Is written off by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: Also requires regularisation after examination by the Public Accounts Committee, like an excess over a voted grant
options.D: Is met automatically from the Contingency Fund of India

e: Excess over a charged appropriation also requires regularisation by Parliament after examination by the Public Accounts Committee, like an excess over a voted grant; charged status only means the expenditure is not voted, not that excess is condoned.

q: The last Railway Budget presented separately to Parliament was the Budget for the year:
e: The Railway Budget was last presented separately for 2016-17; from 2017-18 it was merged with the General Budget.

q: Earnest money and security deposits received from contractors executing railway works are accounted for in:

options.A: The Consolidated Fund of India as revenue receipts
options.B: The Contingency Fund of India
options.D: The Public Account of India, as deposits

e: Earnest money and security deposits received from contractors are not Government revenue but amounts held in trust, so they are accounted for in the Public Account of India as deposits, under the Civil Deposits heads.

q: An increase in capital expenditure on the construction of new lines does not, by itself, worsen the Operating Ratio of a railway because:

options.A: Capital expenditure is not charged to the working expenses of the railway
options.B: Capital expenditure is always met from market borrowings
options.C: Gross traffic earnings rise automatically with capital expenditure
options.D: Dividend is no longer payable to General Finances

e: Operating Ratio relates working expenses to gross traffic earnings; capital expenditure on new lines is charged to capital, not to working expenses, so by itself it does not worsen the Operating Ratio.

q: Unsanctioned expenditure awaiting regularisation is disclosed in the:

options.A: Finance Bill
options.B: Appropriation Accounts
options.D: Demands for Grants

e: Unsanctioned expenditure awaiting regularisation is disclosed in the Appropriation Accounts, which compare actual expenditure with grants and appropriations and bring out such irregularities.

q: Which of the following is NOT a specific instrument of Parliamentary control over public finances?

options.A: Voting of the Demands for Grants by the Lok Sabha
options.B: The Appropriation Act passed by Parliament
options.C: Examination of the accounts and Audit Reports by the Public Accounts Committee
options.D: A Calling Attention motion on a matter of urgent public importance

e: Voting of Demands, the Appropriation Act and PAC examination of accounts and Audit Reports are specific instruments of Parliamentary financial control; a Calling Attention motion is a general parliamentary device, not a specific instrument of financial control.

q: By convention, the Chairperson of the Estimates Committee is appointed by the Speaker from amongst the members of the Committee belonging to:

options.A: The Opposition in the Lok Sabha
options.B: The ruling party (treasury benches) in the Lok Sabha
options.D: The Public Accounts Committee

e: By convention, unlike the Public Accounts Committee whose chairperson is from the Opposition, the Chairperson of the Estimates Committee is appointed by the Speaker from members belonging to the ruling party in the Lok Sabha.

q: In the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, the Suspense Accounts relating specifically to Railways are accounted for under Major Head:
e: In the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, the Suspense Accounts operated specifically by Railways are under Major Head 8660, in the series 8658 (Civil), 8659 (Defence), 8660 (Railways), 8661 (Posts) and 8662 (Telecom).

q: Minor Head 101 under Major Head 8658 – Suspense Accounts is:

options.A: Pay and Accounts Office Suspense
options.B: Public Sector Bank Suspense
options.D: Reserve Bank Suspense – Headquarters

e: Under Major Head 8658 Suspense Accounts, Minor Head 101 is Pay and Accounts Office Suspense, used for initial record of inter-governmental and PAO transactions awaiting settlement.

q: Minor Head 108 under Major Head 8658 – Suspense Accounts, operated for transactions occurring at the accredited public sector banks which are yet to be adjusted in the Central Accounts of the Reserve Bank, is:

options.A: Pay and Accounts Office Suspense
options.B: Public Sector Bank Suspense
options.D: Tax Deducted at Source Suspense

e: Minor Head 108 under Major Head 8658 is Public Sector Bank Suspense, operated for transactions occurring at accredited public sector banks which are yet to be adjusted in the Central Accounts of the Reserve Bank.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Minor Head 109 under Major Head 8658 is Reserve Bank Suspense – Headquarters.
2. Minor Head 110 under Major Head 8658 is Reserve Bank Suspense – Central Accounts Office.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: In the List of Major and Minor Heads, Minor Head 109 under 8658 is Reserve Bank Suspense - Headquarters and Minor Head 110 is Reserve Bank Suspense - Central Accounts Office, so both statements are correct.

q: The amounts placed under the various suspense minor heads below Major Head 8658 are finally cleared from the accounts by:

options.A: Transfer to the Contingency Fund of India
options.B: Writing them off at the close of the financial year
options.C: Charging them to the grant of the following year
options.D: Minus debit or minus credit, as the case may be, on receipt of the relevant information or settlement

e: Amounts under the suspense minor heads below 8658 are finally cleared by minus debit or minus credit, as the case may be, on receipt of the relevant information or settlement, as stated in the notes to the List of Major and Minor Heads.
